title: Severe pneumonia HFNC trial followed by early controlled intubation
label: One reasonable approach
source: FLORALI trial NEJM 2015; Kang BJ et al. ICM 2015; Roca O et al. AJRCCM 2019

decisions.rationale: Escalate from non-rebreather mask to HFNC 60 L/min and FiO2 0.8 to meet high peak inspiratory flow demands and wash out anatomic dead space.
decisions.source: Rochwerg B, et al. ESICM/ERS Guideline on HFNC. Intensive Care Med 2020;46:2226-37

decisions.rationale: Objective blood gas to quantify severe hypoxaemia and calculate baseline ROX index.
Reassessment arterial blood gas during HFNC trial as respiratory rate climbs and ROX index falls.
decisions.source: Roca O, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;199:1368-76

decisions.rationale: Proceed to controlled endotracheal intubation after 2-hour HFNC review shows rising respiratory rate and falling ROX index predicting HFNC failure.
decisions.source: Kang BJ, et al. Failure of high-flow nasal cannula therapy may delay needed intubation and increase mortality. Intensive Care Med 2015;41:623-32

decisions.rationale: Immediate post-intubation lung protective ventilation calibrated to 6 mL/kg predicted body weight (330 mL for 55 kg PBW) with RR 26 bpm to maintain pH and moderate PEEP 10 cmH2O.
decisions.source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023
